frequency_question: How often do major partisan voting bills advance to Senate passage within a 336-day window when initial signals are present?
membership_rule: Includes major standalone federal legislation altering voter registration, ballot access, or election administration that faced intense partisan division; excludes routine appropriations or uncontroversial bipartisan technical corrections.

cases.name: Freedom to Vote Act (S. 1 / S. 2747 attempts)
American Confidence in Elections (ACE) Act push

coverage_note: 4 named historical instances representing polarized electoral reform attempts in modern Senate conditions.
known_gaps: Excludes minor provisions embedded inside omnibus spending bills.
skeleton: Polarized election reform legislative pushes across 6 congressional biennial cycles since the late 1990s where one party holds narrow or split control.
multiplier: 4 major partisan/franchise legislative pushes identified; 2 achieved Senate passage (or identical vehicle success) and 2 failed to clear the Senate threshold.
validity_reason: Remains valid until the conclusion of the current congressional structural alignment and Senate filibuster norms.
